fluff.overview: The Banshee is a medium aerospace fighter designed by Wangker Aerospace for the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth. Introduced in 3046, the BSE-X2 was conceived as an experimental platform intended to dramatically increase the operational flight time of aerospace fighters. The design employed an unconventional dual-engine configuration, pairing a standard fusion powerplant for space operations with a separate turbine engine for atmospheric combat. While this approach demonstrated remarkable potential for extended endurance and surprisingly responsive handling, the combined mass of the two powerplants severely compromised the fighter's acceleration, limiting it to a mere four gravities of thrust. Thin armor protection further compounded the design's shortcomings, leaving the fifty-ton fighter with coverage comparable to craft half its weight. Despite these issues, the Banshee's innovative cockpit systems and dual-motive concept represented a bold if ultimately unsuccessful experiment in aerospace fighter design.
fluff.capabilities:
The Banshee's most distinctive feature is its dual-motive propulsion system. A WAS 150 fusion engine handles space operations while a Wangker 250 Turbine provides power for atmospheric flight. This arrangement gives the fighter exceptional atmospheric endurance compared to purely fusion-driven designs, but the combined weight of both powerplants consumes the majority of the airframe's fifty-ton mass budget, leaving little room for weaponry or protection.

Offensively, the BSE-X2 carries only a pair of Maxell medium lasers, giving it less firepower than even the much lighter Cheetah. Ten single heat sinks manage the modest thermal output of this limited arsenal with ease. Defensively, the fighter's armor coverage is woefully thin, offering protection more consistent with a twenty-five-ton light fighter than a medium-class design.

The cockpit incorporates an innovative computer-directed seat system designed to respond to G-forces during combat maneuvering. As the fighter executes various maneuvers, the computer adjusts the seat position to alleviate pilot stress, squeezing out additional performance from the airframe's limited thrust envelope. The cockpit can also pivot ninety degrees, allowing the Banshee to land virtually anywhere without requiring fixed support infrastructure. The Ranker 200 communications system and Ranker TA 950 targeting and tracking system complete the avionics suite, housed within the Wangker III airframe.
fluff.deployment: The BSE-X2 existed solely as a small number of prototypes and never entered series production. Originally assigned to peripheral garrisons for extended evaluation trials, the existing prototypes saw unexpected combat service during the Clan Invasion era. The design was particularly associated with the 1st Somerset Strikers, an elite unit that operated along the Clan frontier during the early stages of the invasion.
fluff.history:
Wangker Aerospace developed the Banshee during the mid-3040s as part of a broader research initiative to improve aerospace fighter operational endurance. At the time, the company's Axton facility was enjoying a period of revitalization following decades of decline during the Succession Wars, and the dual-motive concept represented an ambitious departure from conventional fighter design philosophy. The BSE-X2 designation reflected its experimental nature, and initial test flights demonstrated the viability of combining fusion and turbine powerplants within a single airframe.

However, the prototype's performance shortcomings quickly became apparent during AFFC evaluation. The fighter's limited acceleration and thin protection made it unsuitable for front-line service against any contemporary opposition. Procurement officers within the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth, reluctant to formally cancel the project and potentially damage their professional relationships with Wangker, instead shuffled the already-built prototypes to remote garrisons along the Periphery border for indefinite extended testing. This maneuver effectively consigned the Banshee to obscurity.

The quiet burial was disrupted by the Clan Invasion of 3049. As the Inner Sphere scrambled to meet the Clan threat, even marginal assets were pressed into service. The Banshee prototypes found themselves in combat against Clan aerospace fighters, where their deficiencies proved even more pronounced. The fighter's sluggish thrust and minimal armament left it hopelessly outclassed against the superior technology and tactics of the invading Clans. Despite these limitations, the design's association with the 1st Somerset Strikers ensured it a small but memorable place in the military history of the Clan Invasion period.

Wangker Aerospace made no further attempts to develop the dual-engine concept, and the BSE-X2 remained an experimental curiosity. The Axton facility instead focused its resources on proven designs like the Corsair, which continued to serve the Federated Suns and its successor states well into the thirty-first century.
